analysis_title: Quantitative Investigation of R6 Plateau and Contrast with R1 Undamped Oscillations

r1_undamped_benchmark.termination_reason: Monotonic coupled divergence from iteration 9 to 23; walltime / timeout exhaustion
r1_undamped_benchmark.active_set_trajectory: Contracted from 13803 to 5664 but remained large (>5600 nodes) with escalating coupled oscillations

spatial_evidence_evaluation.spatial_status_note: EXPLICIT LIMITATION: Solver telemetry in live_iteration_telemetry.json logs only scalar max-norms (delta_d, delta_u, delta_h, KKT errors) and cardinalities (|A|, |F|). Per-node spatial coordinates and spatial localization maps of unconverged damage increments are NOT recorded in the authentic telemetry stream. While fracture mechanics indicates that active-set nodes are localized to the notch root / crack tip, no direct node-resolved spatial evidence exists in the authentic execution log.

mathematical_diagnosis.operator_nature: NON_STATIONARY_ACTIVE_SET_CONVERGENCE_PLATEAU: The observed empirical contraction ratio rho_d ~ 0.9892 cannot be interpreted as an asymptotic spectral radius of a stationary linear operator, because the active set |A_k| is actively shedding nodes at 8.7 nodes/iteration across the final 20 iterations (decreasing monotonically from 334 to 160 nodes). Each active set change alters the Dirichlet/Neumann boundary partition in the phase-field solver. Therefore, the slow convergence is driven by the coupled evolution of the active set boundary rather than asymptotic eigenspace contraction of a fixed map.
mathematical_diagnosis.spectral_radius_qualification: rho ~ 0.989 reflects transient active-set shedding combined with under-relaxed coupled Picard iterations, NOT a static operator spectral radius.
mathematical_diagnosis.damping_assessment: Uniform damping omega_d = 0.5 successfully eliminated the catastrophic divergence observed in R1, enabling 98.84% active set contraction. However, retaining uniform omega_d = 0.5 indefinitely causes extreme convergence deceleration once |A_k| enters the crack-tip plateau.

falsifiable_successor_proposal.description: Two-phase safeguarded relaxation: Stage 1 maintains uniform omega_d = 0.5 until active-set stabilization (|A_k - A_{k-1}| <= 2 for 3 consecutive iterations); Stage 2 activates safeguarded dynamic acceleration (omega_d = 0.85 or Anderson depth m=2) with strict non-healing and residual monotonicity safeguards.
falsifiable_successor_proposal.hypothesis: Uniform damping omega_d = 0.5 is necessary during the rapid active-set contraction phase (|A|: 13,803 -> ~150) to prevent R1-style divergence, but acts as an artificial bottleneck once |A_k| stabilizes near the crack tip, where rho ~ 0.989 would require >700 iterations. Controlled transition to higher relaxation or Anderson acceleration will accelerate convergence to delta_d <= 1e-5 while preserving KKT and coupled equilibrium.
safeguards: Strict non-healing check: max(d_0 - d) <= 1e-6 at every relaxed step.
Rollback mechanism: if delta_d_{k} > 1.05 * delta_d_{k-1} in Stage 2, revert immediately to omega_d = 0.5.
Retain identical coupled equilibrium acceptance criteria: Delta d <= 1e-5, Delta u <= 1e-9 mm, Delta H <= 1e-4 MPa, Force drift <= 2%, Energy drift <= 2%.
falsifiable_successor_proposal.predicted_iterations_to_convergence: 35-50 iterations with acceleration vs >700 iterations under uniform omega_d=0.5.
